documents.title: Attendance Policy
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Attendance Policy
Document ID: UNI-001
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional policy

1. Minimum attendance
Students must maintain at least 75% attendance in each course to qualify for the regular end-semester examination.

2. Attendance calculation
Attendance percentage is calculated as classes attended divided by total classes conducted for the relevant course, multiplied by 100. Attendance is tracked separately for each course.

3. Medical absence requests
A student requesting consideration for medical absence must submit a medical certificate and an application to the Academic Office within five working days of returning to class. Submission does not guarantee approval.

4. Attendance shortage
A student below the minimum attendance threshold must contact the Academic Office to confirm examination eligibility and learn whether any formal remedy is available. Exceptions require written approval from the authorized academic officer.

5. Record correction
Students who believe an attendance entry is incorrect should contact the course instructor with the date and supporting details. The instructor reviews the record and forwards approved corrections to the Academic Office.

This document is fictional and exists only for RAGChat training.

documents.title: Examination Rules
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Examination Rules
Document ID: UNI-002
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional policy

1. Examination eligibility
To sit the regular end-semester examination for a course, a student must meet the attendance requirement in UNI-001 and complete any course-specific assessment requirements announced by the instructor.

2. Identification
Students must bring their university student identity card to an in-person examination. A student who has forgotten the card should report to the examination supervisor before the examination begins and follow the supervisor's instructions.

3. Arrival time
Students should arrive at least 15 minutes before the scheduled start time. Entry after the examination has started is subject to the examination supervisor's decision.

4. Academic integrity
Unauthorized notes, communication devices used for assistance, or collaboration during an individual examination are prohibited. Suspected violations are referred for review under the Student Code of Conduct (UNI-009).

5. Results and review
Results are published through the student portal when approved for release. A student who believes a mark was recorded incorrectly may request a clerical review through the Academic Office within seven calendar days of result publication. A clerical review checks recording and calculation; it is not a re-evaluation of academic judgment.

This document is fictional and exists only for RAGChat training.

documents.title: Grading and Assessment Policy
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Grading and Assessment Policy
Document ID: UNI-003
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional policy

1. Assessment structure
Unless a course outline states otherwise, a course is assessed through 40 marks of continuous assessment and 60 marks in the end-semester examination, for a total of 100 marks.

2. Passing requirement
A student must earn at least 40 marks out of 100 overall and at least 24 out of 60 in the end-semester examination to pass a course.

3. Grade bands
The default grade bands are:
A: 85–100
B: 70–84
C: 55–69
D: 40–54
F: below 40 or failure to meet the minimum end-semester examination requirement.

4. Course-specific rules
An approved course outline may define a different assessment structure if it is published to students before assessment begins. Students should consult their current course outline for any approved variation.

5. Grade questions
Questions about a grade should first be directed to the course instructor. Requests to correct a clerical error may be submitted under the procedure in UNI-002.

This document is fictional and exists only for RAGChat training.

documents.title: Course Registration Policy
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Course Registration Policy
Document ID: UNI-004
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional policy

1. Registration period
For the 2026–27 academic year, the standard course registration window for the first semester is 1–10 July 2026. The standard window for the second semester is 2–10 January 2027.

2. Add or drop a course
Students may request to add or drop a course through the student portal during the first five calendar days after the relevant semester begins. Approval depends on seat availability, prerequisites, and the program's credit requirements.

3. Prerequisites
Students must satisfy the prerequisites listed in the official course catalogue before registering for a course. The registration system may block enrollment when a prerequisite is missing.

4. Credit load
The normal semester load is 18–24 credits. Requests to register for fewer than 18 or more than 24 credits must be reviewed by the program coordinator.

5. Registration help
Students who encounter a portal error should save a screenshot and contact the Registrar's Office. They should not share their password with staff or other students.

documents.title: Tuition Fee and Payment Policy
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Tuition Fee and Payment Policy
Document ID: UNI-005
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional policy

1. Undergraduate tuition
The standard undergraduate tuition fee is INR 85,000 per semester for the 2026–27 academic year. Program-specific fees, if any, are listed in the student's admission letter.

2. Payment deadlines
For the 2026–27 academic year, the standard payment deadline is 15 July 2026 for the first semester and 15 January 2027 for the second semester.

3. Late payment charge
Unless an approved extension or documented exception applies, a late payment charge of INR 500 is applied after the deadline, followed by INR 100 for each subsequent calendar day that the balance remains unpaid.

4. Payment methods
Students can pay through the university student portal using the payment methods displayed there. Students should retain the transaction receipt until the payment appears in their account statement.

5. Fee refunds
This policy does not define hostel fee refunds, travel reimbursements, or refunds for optional extracurricular activities. Students seeking information on those topics should contact the Finance Office.

documents.title: Scholarship Policy
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Scholarship Policy
Document ID: UNI-006
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional policy

1. Merit scholarship eligibility
New undergraduate students with a score of at least 90% in the qualifying examination may apply for the Northstar Merit Scholarship. Meeting the threshold permits an application but does not guarantee an award.

2. Scholarship value
The standard Northstar Merit Scholarship covers 25% of undergraduate tuition for one academic year. It does not automatically cover accommodation, meals, transport, or other personal expenses.

3. Application documents
Applicants must submit the scholarship form, qualifying examination result, proof of admission, and a student identity document through the scholarship portal by the deadline shown on that portal.

4. Renewal
Renewal is assessed annually. Students must maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5 on the university's 4.0 scale and complete all required credits for the academic year. Renewal remains subject to verification and available funding.

5. Other financial aid
This document describes only the Northstar Merit Scholarship. It does not specify eligibility or amounts for need-based grants, emergency loans, or external scholarships. Contact the Student Support Office for those programs.

documents.title: Student Leave and Absence Procedure
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Student Leave and Absence Procedure
Document ID: UNI-007
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional policy

1. Planned absence
Students expecting to miss classes should inform the course instructor in advance where possible. Informing an instructor does not automatically convert an absence into attended class time.

2. Medical absence
A student seeking consideration for medical absence must submit a medical certificate and application to the Academic Office within five working days of returning to class. The request is reviewed individually and may be approved or declined.

3. Personal leave
Students may submit a personal leave request to the program coordinator. Approval depends on the circumstances and does not guarantee an attendance exemption.

4. Supporting documents
Students should provide documents that are relevant to the request and should submit them through the official student portal or directly to the office named in the relevant procedure. Students should not send sensitive medical details to unrelated staff.

5. Attendance impact
Approved leave does not automatically change the attendance percentage. Attendance records and examination eligibility remain governed by UNI-001 and UNI-002.

documents.title: Library and Campus Facilities Guide
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Library and Campus Facilities Guide
Document ID: UNI-008
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional guide

1. Main library hours
During teaching weeks, the main library is open Monday through Friday from 08:00 to 20:00 and Saturday from 09:00 to 16:00. It is closed on Sundays and published university holidays.

2. Borrowing books
Undergraduate students may borrow up to four books at a time for 14 calendar days. Books may be renewed once if no other user has reserved them.

3. Computer laboratories
The general computer laboratories are open Monday through Friday from 09:00 to 18:00 during teaching weeks. Access may be restricted during scheduled classes, maintenance, or examinations.

4. Student help desk
The campus help desk is located in the Student Services Building and operates Monday through Friday from 09:00 to 17:00, excluding published university holidays.

5. Accessibility and equipment
Students who need accessible study arrangements or specialized equipment should contact Student Services at least three working days before the intended visit. Availability must be confirmed by the office.

documents.title: Student Code of Conduct
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Student Code of Conduct
Document ID: UNI-009
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional policy

1. Respectful conduct
Students are expected to treat other students, staff, visitors, and campus workers respectfully and must not engage in harassment, threats, or discriminatory conduct.

2. Academic integrity
Plagiarism, fabrication of academic work, unauthorized collaboration, and use of prohibited materials during assessments are academic integrity violations.

3. Reporting a concern
A student may report a concern to the Student Conduct Office or through the official student portal. Reports should include a clear description of the incident and any relevant evidence. Reports are handled confidentially to the extent possible under the review process.

4. Review process
The university reviews reported concerns before deciding whether a policy violation occurred. Students involved in a review will be informed of the applicable process and given an opportunity to respond.

5. Possible outcomes
Depending on the findings and severity, outcomes may include an educational warning, required training, a formal reprimand, or suspension under the university's disciplinary procedure. No outcome is automatic; decisions depend on the case.

documents.title: Academic Calendar 2026–27
documents.content:
NORTHSTAR UNIVERSITY
Academic Calendar 2026–27
Document ID: UNI-010
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 1 July 2026
Status: Official fictional calendar

1. First semester
The first semester begins on 20 July 2026. The teaching period runs from 20 July through 20 November 2026. The regular end-semester examination period is scheduled for 30 November through 12 December 2026.

2. Second semester
The second semester begins on 18 January 2027. The teaching period runs from 18 January through 21 May 2027. The regular end-semester examination period is scheduled for 31 May through 12 June 2027.

3. Mid-semester break
The scheduled mid-semester break for the first semester is 12–16 October 2026. The scheduled mid-semester break for the second semester is 15–19 March 2027.

4. Public holidays and updates
Individual public holidays and any calendar changes are announced through the student portal. Students should check the portal for the latest notices before making travel plans.

5. Calendar scope
This calendar lists the main semester dates. It does not list every course-specific deadline, assignment due date, or individual examination timetable. Those details are published separately by the relevant department or instructor.
